column3: title card: a plugin's dictionary, for developers (ERP_FRIENDLY_OPS_LENS.md §22-§23)
column5: F: For developers: a plugin's dictionary. | M: How Libero ships its dictionary rows the iDempiere way, as 2Packs, and what Start, reload and Stop do with them.

M: In iDempiere, Libero's dictionary sits in its 2Pack zips, and the Incremental 2Pack Activator applies each pack above the installed version, once. | F: Here the manifest lists the same three packs plus our own, one point zero point three. Callouts come per table and column, and Stop leaves the rows.

column5: F: Start runs the Pack In, before any plugin code. | M: Pack one point zero: five thousand ninety-six records; the two thousand eight hundred sixty official ones are skipped, as iDempiere does, and three hundred seventy-four go in. Its four functions and eight views are not in the twin yet, and are reported by name. | F: Then the class renames, the callout clean-up, and our process and button. A new process gets access for every automatic role: twelve rows.
M: Packages Installed: four packs, each completed successfully, where an iDempiere administrator looks for them.

column5: F: Report and Process: our packed process. Its id comes from the sequence, it is found by its UUID. | M: Report Access shows System's own two rows; across all tenants there are twelve, one per automatic role. | F: And pack one point zero point two cleared the eighteen column callouts named after the old classes. Libero registers them again per table and column, as its plugin dot xml does, so the order form still fills itself.

column5: M: The dictionary is rebuilt from the seed at every load. | F: So the four hundred eighty-four writes the packs made are replayed first, in milliseconds. A changed seed means a full Pack In instead, in seconds. And Start in this session applies nothing: the packs are installed.
